record.issue_text: [BUG] createEvent now selects the target calendar solely via `destinationCalendar.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)` with a `|| "primary"` fallback, so a destination calendar whose credentialId is null never matches any credential. Users whose DestinationCalendar row has no credentialId — a state the old EventManager explicitly branched for and the old code served via externalId — get every event created on their Google primary calendar instead of the configured destination calendar.

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent`, the target `calendarId` is now chosen only via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` and otherwise falls back to `"primary"` (see `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`). But `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` explicitly supports destination calendars with *no* `credentialId` (the `else` branch when `destination.credentialId` is falsy) and still passes the same `event` containing destinationCalendar entries that may have `credentialId` unset. In that case, Google createEvent will never find a matching destination calendar and will create the event on the primary calendar instead of the configured destination calendar externalId—whereas the old code used `destinationCalendar.externalId` directly regardless of credentialId.
